clue.text: Skip country of origin of beauty queen

parts.note: to skip a lesson is to miss it
for this English newspaper's readers, the home country is England

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave out the homeland of a pageant winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skip' reads as an order to leave something out, but it simply supplies MISS; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A national beauty contest crowns a winner titled with her country's name, here the English champion.

clue.text: Don't rely on fog and corrosion

parts.note: fog is thick mist
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Advice not to trust damp weather and rot.
explanation.definitionFit: To lack confidence in something and so not depend on it is to doubt it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rank of deputy German leader

parts.note: a deputy is a stand-in, someone who takes another's place

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the head of German

explanation.surface: The status of a deputy who leads in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German leader' suggests a chancellor, but 'leader' only asks for the first letter of 'German'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's rank is their status or position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: The Spanish part of fish is small and mischievously charming

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'
a fin is part of a fish

explanation.surface: A bit of Spanish seafood described as dainty and impish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small and impish, so something elf-like is tiny and full of playful charm.

clue.text: Down to earth attraction

parts.note: the pull that draws things down towards the earth, read literally rather than as 'practical appeal'

explanation.surface: The appeal of someone sensible and unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down to earth' usually means unpretentious; here it is literal, the direction of the force.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics names the mutual pulling force between masses, which makes dropped objects fall to the ground.

clue.text: Opposed to a profit on the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another stands above it

parts.note: a profit is a gain
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone objects to making money while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hostile or in opposition to something is a direct synonym of the preposition.

clue.text: In which one is obliged to tax a vault

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
to vault is to leap, and a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Being made to pay tax on a burial vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests a cellar or tomb; here it is a jump, a bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under a moral or legal obligation to do something is the state described.

clue.text: Strike back at standard

indicators.note: back tells us the word for strike is read from right to left

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: Hitting out at the norm in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike back' looks like retaliation; 'back' reverses RAP, and 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the accepted normal level, as in golf or 'up to par'.

clue.text: Almost exact summary

indicators.note: almost tells us the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: precise means exact

explanation.surface: A nearly accurate short account.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a brief abridged version of a text, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Split on female for choice

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another stands above it

parts.note: to split on someone is to inform on them, to rat
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone betrays a woman because they prefer to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split on' reads as one phrasal verb meaning to betray, but the clue uses 'Split' alone for informing and 'on' as the down-clue placement.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something by preference is to do it sooner, as in 'I would prefer to'.

clue.text: Mark has fresh start for preventing a pain in the neck

definitions.text: for preventing a pain in the neck

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so take the opening of fresh

explanation.surface: A scarred person makes a new beginning to avoid an annoying neck ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pain in the neck' usually means a nuisance; here it is literal stiffness from cold, which a wrap prevents.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen neckwear item keeps the throat warm against chills that cause a stiff neck.

clue.text: A section intended, we hear, for the flat

parts.note: a part is a section

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for intended is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A portion said to be set aside as a residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns MEANT into MENT, which sounds the same; 'for the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms on one floor, the American term for the same dwelling.

clue.text: Officer blushing to reach standard afloat

parts.note: someone blushing goes red
an ensign is a junior officer

explanation.surface: A junior officer turns red on meeting the expected level aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' here is a flag, not a level of quality; 'to reach' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The British merchant navy's flag is a standard flown at sea.

clue.text: Shade turns out to be one returning for example

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: returning tells us the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A colour proves, on checking, to be a recurring instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses EG to GE; 'turns out' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a colour, and this one is a pale sandy brown.

clue.text: Stranded youth setting a happy standard

definitions.text: Stranded youth setting a happy standard

parts.words: Stranded youth setting a happy standard
parts.note: a lad on the strand, the beach, who is the model of cheerfulness in a well-known saying

explanation.surface: A marooned young man stays cheerful as an example to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy as a sandboy' is a British saying for being carefree; 'Stranded' means on the strand, or beach, not abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The British simile 'happy as a sandboy' makes this boy the byword for cheerfulness.

clue.text: Stop offer being made to hotel worker

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: A hotel employee is prevented from making a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being made to' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who serves drinks in a hotel's bar is one of its staff.

clue.text: Solicitor in East-end dismissed

indicators.note: the end of East is its last letter

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A London lawyer from the East End has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer; here it is someone who solicits custom. 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tout pesters people for business, selling tickets or custom, so he solicits.

clue.text: A vault round doctor with deadly weapon

parts.note: a vault is a burial chamber, a tomb
O is round in shape
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor in a crypt with a lethal arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear explosive device is the deadliest weapon of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Part of church making strange patterns

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of patterns are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A section of a church produces odd designs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cross-shaped church, the arms crossing the nave are its transepts.

clue.text: Verbal dexterity outside right finds in summons

indicators.note: outside means the word for verbal dexterity is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: wit is cleverness with words

explanation.surface: Clever wordplay going right finds its way into a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's written order commanding someone to appear is a summons.

clue.text: Fell and grasped what meaning there was

definitions.meaning: to tumble to something is to realise or understand it

explanation.surface: Someone took a fall and understood what little sense there was.
explanation.definitionFit: Toppled over describes a fall; 'tumbled to' is idiom for suddenly understanding.

clue.text: Book reviewer in company is all ears

definitions.meaning: a firm's accounts, its books, are checked by an independent reviewer
someone all ears is listening intently, a hearer

explanation.surface: A literary critic at a firm pays close attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book reviewer' suggests a critic, but the books are accounts; 'is' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant checking a firm's accounts carries this title, and in Latin it also means a hearer or listener.

clue.text: Last word about a divine bachelor with nothing on his belly'!

indicators.note: about means the last word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
BD, Bachelor of Divinity, is a degree for a divine
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A naked clergyman's final word about his stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on his' are links; 'a' is a link before the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach region of the body is the belly.

clue.text: Odds one obtained for Peg controlling flow of liquor

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
I is the Roman numeral one
got means obtained

explanation.surface: Betting odds won a drinker a peg of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the British betting term for the odds when a race begins; 'for' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap or stopper fitted in a cask controls how its contents run out.

clue.text: Tasty morsel accountant gets on back of neck

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another stands above it

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
the nape is the back of the neck

explanation.surface: An accountant gets food on his collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury snack on bread served at parties is a tasty bite.

clue.text: It's used for evening form of transport

definitions.meaning: a carpenter's tool for making a surface level, evening it

explanation.surface: Something used for a night out, a way of travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is not the time of day but making even.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking tool smooths timber flat; the same word is short for an aircraft.

clue.text: Trader who doesn't go to extremes

definitions.text: Trader who doesn't go to extremes

parts.words: Trader who doesn't go to extremes
parts.note: a dealer who stays in the centre, read literally as someone positioned between two ends

explanation.surface: A moderate merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary dealer stands between producer and buyer, literally in the middle position.

clue.text: Hound controller with the French hard wood

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
ash is a hard wood

explanation.surface: A dog lead made of tough French timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog lead restrains a hound, so it controls the animal.

clue.text: Winning everything during big fight

parts.note: grand means big
a slam is a heavy blow or attack, as in a fight

explanation.surface: A clean sweep achieved in a major bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or tennis, taking every trick or every major title is a complete sweep.

clue.text: Make up an accent

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
a tone is an accent or manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Putting on a particular way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' looks like inventing or cosmetics; here it is making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up for a wrong is to make amends for it.

clue.text: Draw a bond

definitions.meaning: a draw is a match with level scores
a bond or link joining people

explanation.surface: A drawn match, a connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A level result is a stalemate in sport; a link between people is a connection.

clue.text: Part of Yorkshire by custom making horsy clothes

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings
a habit is a custom

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire district's traditional outfit for equestrians.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was once split into three Ridings (North, East, West); 'by' and 'making' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's outfit for horseback, jacket and skirt, is worn when going out on horseback.
